我们关于空间和时间的体系由两个密切联系着的部分组成。
第一个部分依赖于这个系列推理：心灵的能力不是无限的；因此任何广延或持续的观念都不是由无数的部分或较小的观念组成，
而是由这些数目有限并且是简单而不可分割的观念组成的。因此，空间和时间就可能是与这个观念相符合才得以存在的；而如果是可能的，它们就必然是在事实上与这个观念相符合才得以存在的，因为它们的无限可分性是完全不可能和矛盾的。
我们体系的另一个部分是上面这个部分的结果。空间和时间的观念分解自身而成的这些部分最终成了不可分的；如果它们不是被一些真实的和存在着的对象充满着，这些自身为不存在的东西

The ideas of space and time are therefore no separate or distinct ide-
as, but merely those of the manner or order, in which objects exist:
Or, in other words, ′ tis impossible to conceive either a vacuum and
extension without matter, or a time, when there was no succession or
change in any real existence. The intimate connexion betwixt these
parts of our system is the reason why we shall examine together the
objections, which have been urg’ d against both of them, beginning
with those against the finite divisibility of extension.
I. The first of these objections, which I shall take notice of, is
more proper to prove this connexion and dependance of the one part
upon the other, than to destroy either of them. It has often becn main-
tain’ d in the schools, that extension must be divisible, in infinitum,
because the system of mathematical points is absurd; and that system
is absurd, because a mathematical point is a non-entity, and conse-
quently can never by its conjunction with others form a real existence.
This wou’ d be perfectly decisive, were there no medium betwixt the
infinite divisibility of matter, and the non-entity of mathematical
points. But there is evidently a medium, viz. the bestowing a colour or
solidity on these points; and the absurdity of both the extremes is a
demonstration of the truth and reality of this medium. The system of
physical points, which is another medium, is too absurd to need a ref-
utation. A real extension, such as a physical point is suppos' d to be ,
can never exist without parts, different from each other; and wherever
objects are different , they are distinguishable and separable by the i-
magination,
I1.The second objection is deriv'd from the necessity there
wou′ d be of penetration, if extension consisted of mathematical points.
A simple and indivisible atom, that touches another, must necessarily
penetrate it; for'tis impossible it can touch it by its extermal parts, from
the very supposition of its perfect simplicity, which excludes all parts.

的不可分的部分将是难以想象的。因此，空间和时间观念不是各自分离或不同的观念，而仅仅是那些对象存在的方式或次序的观念。或者，换句话说，我们不可能设想出没有物质的真空和广延，
或者设想出在任何真实存在者中都没有接续或变化的时间。由于我们的理论体系的这些部分之间的密切联系，我们将对那些关于它们的反驳一并加以考察，首先考察的就是关于反对广延的有限可分说的那些反驳。
1.我所关注的第一个反驳，更适合于去证明一个部分对另一个部分的联系和依赖，而不是去摧毁它们中的任何一个。在一些学派中常常会有人主张广延必定是无限可分的，因为数学点这一理论体系是荒谬的。之所以这个理论体系是荒谬的，乃是因为数学点是一个非实体，因此它绝不可能通过和其他数学点的联结形成一个真实的存在。如果在物质的无限可分性和数学点的非实体之间没有一个中介，这种反驳将绝对是决定性的。但这里明显有一个中介，也即这些点所赋予的颜色或坚固性；两个极端的荒谬性证明了这个中介的正确性和真实性。物理点这个理论体系是另一个中介，它极端荒谬，并不需要对其进行驳斥。正如物理点被假定的那样，一个真正的广延永远不能没有相互差异的部分而存在；而只要对象是差异的，它们就能够为想象所区别和分离。
Ⅱ.第二个反驳来自于这样一种需要：如果广延是由数学点组成的，那它们就一定是互相渗透的。一个简单而不可分割的原子接触另一个原子时，必定会渗透到它的里面。因为根据它是完全简单的、就会把所有的部分排斥掉这样的假定，它就不能借助于它外在的部分接触另一个原子。因此，第一个原子和另一一81一

It must therefore touch it intimately,and in its whole essence, secun-
dum se, tota，& totaliter; which is the very definition of penetration.
But penetration is impossible; Mathematical points are of consequence
equally impossible.
I answer this objection by substituting a juster idea of penetra-
tion. Suppose two bodies containing no void within. their circumfer-
ence, to approach each other, and to unite in such a manner that the
body, which results from their union, is no more extended than either
of them;’tis this we must mean when we talk of penetration. But'’tis
evident this penetration is nothing but the annihilation of one of these
bodies, and the preservation of the other, without our being able to
distinguish particularly which is preserv′ d and which annihilated. Be-
fore the approach we have the idea of two bodies. After it we have the
idea only of one. ′Tis impossible for the mind to preserve any notion
of difference betwixt two bodies of the same nature existing in the
same place at the same time.
Taking then penetration in this sense, for the annihilation of one
body upon its approach to another, I ask any one, if he sees a neces-
sity , that a colour′ d or tangible point shou′ d be annihilated upon the
approach of another colour’ d or tangible point? On the contrary,
does he not evidently perceive, that from the union of these points
there results an object, which is compounded and divisible, and may
be distinguish’d into two parts, of which each preserves its existence
distinct and separate, notwithstanding its contiguity to the other? Let
him aid his fancy by conceiving these points to be of different colours,
the better to prevent their coalition and confusion. A blue and a red
point may surely lie contiguous without any penetration or annihila-
tion. For if they cannot, what possibly can become of them ? Whether
shall the red or the blue be annihilated ? Or if these colours unite in-
to one, what new colour will they produce by their union ?

个必定是密切地接触着，并且接触到了它的整个本质（secundu
mse，tota，& totaliter），这就是渗透的恰当定义。但是渗透是不可能的，因此数学点也同样是不可能的。
我通过替换一个更为恰当的渗透观念来答复这个反驳。假定在其周围没有任何空隙的两个物体彼此接近，并且使得以这样的方式将二者联结而成的物体都不比它们中的任何一个占据更大的范围；这应当是我们谈到渗透时的意义。但是，显然的是，这种渗透仅仅指的是两个物体中的一个被消灭，面另一个被保存了，而且我们无法辨别到底哪个被保存了，哪个被消灭了。在它们接触前，我们有两个物体的观念。在接触后，我们仅仅有一个物体的观念。对于这样两个有相同性质，并且在同一地点、同一时间中存在的物体，人们心灵中不可能保存它们之间任何差异的概念。
如果是从一个物体在接触另一个物体时自身就会消灭这种意义上来考虑渗透，我就要问任何人，当一个有颜色或可触知的点在接近另一个有颜色或可触知的点之后，他是否会认为它一定会消灭？正相反，他难道不是明显地察觉到，这些点的相互联结产生了一个复合的和可分的对象么？难道这个对象不是可以区分为尽管彼此邻近，但各自仍保存它们的不同和分离存在的两个部分么？为了更好地防止这两个点混为一体和相互混淆，他可以设想它们有着不同颜色，借以帮助他的想象。的确，一个蓝色的点和一个红色的点可以互相接触，而没有任何渗透或消灭。因为如果它们不能如此，那它们肯会变成什么呢？是红色的点被消灭，还是蓝色的点被消灭？如果这两种颜色结合成了一种，那它们的结合将会产生什么新的颜色呢？

What chiefly gives rise to these objections, and at the same time
renders it so difficult to give a satisfactory answer to them, is the nat-
ural infirmity and unsteadiness both of our imagination and senses,
when employ’d on such minute objcts. Put a spot of ink upon paper,
and retire to such a distance, that the spot becomes altogether invisi-
ble ; you will find, that upon your returm and nearer approach the spot
first becomes visible by short intervals; and afterwards becomes al-
ways visible; and afterwards acquires only a new force in its colouring
without augmenting its bulk; and afterwards, when it has encreas′ d
to such a degree as to be really extended, ' tis still difficult for the i-
magination to break it into its component parts, because of the uneasi-
ness it finds in the conception of such a minute object as a single
point. This infirmity affects most of our reasonings on the present sub-
ject, and makes it almost impossible to answer in an intelligible man-
ner, and in proper expressions, many questions which may arise con-
cerming it.
III. There have been many objections drawn from the mathemat
ics against the indivisibility of the parts of extension; tho’ at first sight
that science seems rather favourable to the present doctrine; and if it
be contrary in its demonstrations,' tis perfectly conformable in its def-
initions. My present business then must be to defend the definitions,
and refute the demonstrations.
A surface is defin'd to be length and breadth without depth : A
line to be length without breadth or depth:A point to be what has nei-
ther length, breadth nor depth. * Tis evident that all this is perfectly
unintelligible upon any other supposition than that of the composition
of extension by indivisible points or atoms. How else cou'd any thing
exist without length, without breadth, or without depth ?
Two different answers, I find, have been made to this argu-
ment; neither of which is in my opinion satisfactory. The first is,
that the objects of geometry, those surfaces, lines and points, whose
proportions and positions it examines, are mere ideas in the mind;

引起这些反驳，同时很难对这些反驳给出一个令人满意的答复的主要原因在于：在运用于这样细微的对象时，我们的想象和感官有一种天然的弱点和不稳定性。在纸上涂一个墨点，然后往后退一段距离，直到完全看不到那个点；你将会发现，在你返回来并且走近墨点时，墨点开始时是时隐时现；然后就变得总是可见；
然后，墨点的体积并未增大，仅仅是它的颜色变得更浓了些；再然后，当它增加到如此的程度，乃至好像它的范围是真正扩大时，想象仍然很难将它分裂为它的组成部分，因为在构思中，很难发现如一个单一的点那样细微的对象。这个弱点影响了我们关于当前这个主题的大部分推理，并使得我们几乎不可能用一种能被理解的方式和恰当的表达答复关于这个主题所可以发生的许多问题。
IⅢI.许多对广延的部分的不可分学说的反驳都是来自于数学，虽然乍一看这门科学似乎更有利于目前这种学说；而且即使在其证明方面数学和目前这种学说是相反的，在其定义方面它却是完全和现在这种学说相符合的。因而，我当前的任务就是必须对这一定义进行辩护，同时对这种证明加以驳斥。
个面被定义为只有长度和宽度，没有厚度；一条线被定义为只有长度，没有宽度或厚度；一个点则被定义为既没有长度，没有宽度，也没有厚度。显而易见，所有这类说法如果不是根据厂延是由不可分割的点或原子组成的这一假定，而是根据其他的假定，那它将是完全不可理解的。难道还有任何其他的没有长度、
没有宽度或没有厚度的东西存在吗？
我发现，对于这个争论，有过两种不同的答复；而在我看来，
这两种答复都不是令人满意的。第一种答复就是：几何学的对象，也即几何学研究它们的比例和位置的那些面、线和点，都只是心一85一

and not only never did, but never can exist in nature. They never did
exist; for no one will pretend to draw a line or make a surface entirely
conformable to the definition : They never can exist; for we may pro-
duce demonstrations from these very ideas to prove that they are im-
possible.
But can any thing be imagin′ d more absurd and contradictory
than this reasoning? Whatever can be conceiv'd by a clear and dis-
tinct idea necessarily implies the posibility of existence; and he who
pretends to prove the impossibility of its existence by any argument
deriv’ d from the clear idea, in reality asserts, that we have no clear
idea of it, because we have a clear idea. 'Tis in vain to search for a
contradiction in any thing that is distinctly conceiv' d by the mind.
Did it imply any contradiction,′ tis impossible it cou'd ever be con-
ceiv' d.
There is therefore no medium betwixt allowing at least the possi-
bility of indivisible points, and denying their idea; and’ tis on this
latter principle, that the second answer to the foregoing argument is
founded. It has been pretended ,that tho′ it be impossible to con-

towns, and overlook its breadth. The length is inseparable from the

中的一些观念而已；它们在自然界中不仅从未存在过，而且也永远不可能存在。它们从未存在过，这是因为没有人自称他们能画出与定义完全一致的一条线或作出与定义完全一致的一个面；它们永远不可能存在，这是因为我们可以从这些恰当的观念中提出实证来证明它们是不可能的。
但是，我们还能想象出比这种推理更为荒谬和矛盾的其他任何事情吗？凡是能被一个清楚和明晰的观念所设想的东西都必定包含着它的存在的可能性；如果一个人自称可以通过由这个清楚的观念而来的任何论证去证明它的存在的不可能性，那实际上他就是在宣称，我们对那个东西没有一个清楚的观念，因为我们有一个清楚的观念。如果想在能为心灵所明晰地设想的任何事物中找出矛盾，那是徒然的。如果它包含任何矛盾，那它就永远不可能被设想。
因此，在至少是承认不可分的点的可能性和否认这种点的观念之间没有任何中介；根据后面的这一原理，建立了对前述论证的第二个答复。有人曾经说过，①尽管不可能设想出没有任何宽度的长度，但是通过一种不必把二署分离的抽象观念，我们能够考虑其中的一个，而不用考虑另外的一个；根据同样的方式，我们可以考虑在两个城镇间的道路的长度，而忽略它的宽度。长度和宽度在自然界和在我们心灵中都是不可分离的，但根据上面解释的那种方式，并不排斥对上述问题作一种片面的考虑和一种理性的区分。
在反驳这个答复时，我并不坚持我已经充分解释过的那个
①思维术。

for the mind to arrive at a minimum in its ideas, its capacity must be
infinite , in order to comprehend the infinite number of parts, of which
its idea of any extension wou′ d be compos’ d. I shall here endeavour
to find some new absurdities in this reasoning.
A surface terminates a solid; a line terminates a surface; a point
terminates a line; but I assert, that if the ideas of a point, line or sur-
face were not indivisible,′ tis impossible we shou' d ever conceive
these terminations. For let these ideas be suppos' d infinitely divisi-
ble; and then let the fancy endeavour to fix itself on the idea of the
last surface, line or point ; it immediately finds this idea to break into
parts; and upon its seizing the last of these parts, it loses its hold by
a new division, and so on in infinitum, without any possibility of its
arriving at a concluding idea. The number of fractions bring it no nea-
rer the last division, than the first idea it form' d. Every particle e-
ludes the grasp by a new fraction; like quicksilver, when we endeav-
our to seize it. But as in fact there must be something, which termi-
nates the idea of every finite quantity; and as this terminating idea
cannot itself consist of parts or inferior ideas; otherwise it wou' d be
the last of its parts, which finish' d the idea, and so on; this is a
clear proof, that the ideas of surfaces, lines and points admit not of
any division; those of surfaces in depth; of lines in breadth and
depth; and of points in any dimension
The schoolmen were so sensible of the force of this argu-

mong those particles of matter, which are divisible in infinitum,
a number of mathematical points, in order to give a termination
to bodies; and others eluded the force of this reasoning by a
heap of unintelligible cavils and distinctions. Both these adversaries

论证，也即，如果心灵在它的观念方面不能达到一个最小值，那么为了包含它的任何广延观念组成的无数的部分，心灵的能力必定是无限的。在这里，我将竭力在上述推理中发现一些新的谬论。
一个面是一个立体的界限，一条线是一个面的界限，一个点是一条线的界限。但是我断言，如果一个点、一条线或一个面的观念不是不可分割的，那我们就永远不可能设想出这些界限。因为如果假定这些观念是无限可分的，然后再使想象将自身固定在最后的面、线或点的观念上，想象就会立刻发现，这个最后的观念分裂成了一些部分，而当它抓住这些部分的最后一个时，又会由于一次薪的分裂而失去，无限地这样下去，想象就永不可能到达一个最后的观念。无论分裂的次数有多少，都比不上为想象所形成的最初观念带给想象更接近于最后的分裂。每一个微粒都因为一次薪的分裂而无法抓住；正如我们竭力去抓住水银的情形一样。但事实上，由于对每一个有限的数量观念来说，必定要有某一个观念来作为它的界限，而且这个界限观念本身不能再由一些部分或较小的观念组成，否则就会是它的最后部分成为观念的界限，如此就可以无限地推下去。这是面、线和点的观念不容许有任何再分的一个清楚的证据；面的观念在厚度上不能再分，线的观念在宽度和厚度上不能再分，而点的观念在长度、宽度和厚度任何一方面都不能再分。
经院派暂学家们强烈地感觉到了这种论证的力量，以至他们中的一些人主张，为了给物体一个界限，在那些可以无限分割的物质微粒中间，自然界已经混合了一些数学点；其他一些人则通过一大堆莫明其妙的挑剔和区分来躲避这种推理的力量。

Thus it appears, that the definitions of mathematics destroy the
pretended demonstrations; and that if we have the idea of indivisible
points, lines and surfaces conformable to the definition, their exist-
ence is certainly possible; but if we have no such idea,' tis impossi
ble we can ever conceive the termination of any figure; without which
conception there can be no geometrical demonstration.
But I go farther, and maintain, that none of these demonstrations
can have sufficient weight to establish such a principle, as this of infi-
nite divisibility; and that because with regard to such minute objects,
they are not properly demonstrations, being built on ideas, which are
not exact, and maxims, which are not precisely true. When geometry
decides any thing concerming the proportions of quantity , we ought not
to look for the utmost precision and exactness. None of its proofs ex-
tend so far. It takes the dimensions and proportions of figures justly;
but roughly,and with some liberty. Its errors are never considerable;
nor wou' d it err at all, did it not aspire to such an absolute perfec-
tion.
I first ask mathematicians, what they mean when they say one
line or surface is EQUAL to, or GREATER, or LESS than another ?
Let any of them give an answer, to whatever sect he belongs, and
whether he maintains the composition of extension by indivisible
points, or by quantities divisible in infinitum. This question will em-
barrass both of them.
There are few or no mathematicians who defend the hypothesis of
indivisible points; and yet these have the readiest and justest answer
to the present question. They need only reply, that fines or surfaces
are equal, when the numbers of points in each are equal; and that
as the proportion of the numbers varies, the proportion of the lines

这两类敌手都同样地认输了。一个躲藏起来的人和一个公然交出其武器的人一样，明显都是承认了他的敌人的优势。
由此看来，数学的定义摧毁了那些伪称的证明。如果我们有与其定义完全一致的不可分的点、线和面的观念，那它们的存在就的确是有可能的；但是如果我们没有这样的观念，我们就永远不可能设想出任何一个形的界限；而如果没有了形的概念，就不可能有任何几何学的证明。
但是，我可以进一步地主张，这些实证没有一个有足够的力量去建构像无限可分说这样的一个原理，这是由于这些实证所依赖的观念并不精确，同时它们所依赖的公理也并不正确，所以它们并不是关于这些微小的对象的恰当的实证。当几何学决定任何关于数量的比例的事物时，我们不应当寻求极端的确切和精确。没有一个几何学的明证能达到这样的程度。它正确地但同时又只是概略地，而且是有些任意地获取了形的尺度和比例。几何学的错误从来都是不值得考虑的，而且如果它不是追求达到那样一种绝对的完美，它就根本不会有错误。
首先，我要问数学家们，当他们说一条线或一个面等于、大于或小于另一条线或另一个面时，他们的意思是什么？任何一位数学家，无论他属于哪个学派，无论他给出的回答是主张广延是由不可分的点组成的，还是由无限可分的数量组成的，这个问题都会令他们感到困窘。
很少或完全没有数学家对不可分的点这一假说进行辩护，然而他们对目前这个问题给出了最现成和最有根据的答案。他们仅仅需要答复说：当一些线或面的点的数目是相等时，这些线或面就是相等的；面且线和面的比例乃是随着点的数

and surfaces is also vary’ d. But tho′ this answer be just, as well as
obvious; yet I may affrm, that this standard of equality is entirely
useless, and that it never is from such a comparison we determine ob-
jects to be equal or unequal with respect to each other. For as the
